svg.text: Library › A Philosophy of Software Design › Notebook
Complexity is whatever makes a system hard to understand or change;
it is measured by the people who work in it, not by the code.

text.tspan: Complexity is a reader's cost, not a size.

svg.text: Dependencies and obscurity are the two causes; the rest are symptoms.

text.tspan: Are there really only two? Where does churn go?

svg.text: A deep module hides far more than it shows, so the people who call it
learn little and get a great deal.

text.tspan: Depth: what it hides minus what it asks

svg.text: the common case should be the simplest thing to call.
A class whose methods only pass their arguments on to another class
adds an interface and hides nothing.
A preview. Nothing is written until you create it.

Opened from the Library (a book's detail, Notebook) and from the
Reader (Contents, then Notebook). Esc goes back to where you were.
The book at a glance: its cover, title, author and how much you marked.
Filter by colour, with counts, or keep only what has a note under it.
Grouped by chapter, in the order of the book.
Each entry: its colour as a bar, the passage, your note, the page and the
chapter. Open in reader goes to the passage; To note starts a note from it.
One primary action: Export as a reading note.
The preview is plain Markdown, no YAML: a title, Source:: to the book,
then per chapter its quotes (> with their page) and your notes as bullets.
Create note writes it, and only then (§XII): Cancel leaves the vault as it
was. The write is recorded, with Undo in Recent.
On a phone: chips scroll, the export button stays at the bottom, and the
preview opens as a sheet with Create note under your thumb.
